title: Talaffuz: urg‘u, ohang va bog‘lanish
goal_uz: Dars oxirida siz so‘z va gap urg‘usini to‘g‘ri qo‘yasiz, kuchsiz shakllar va bog‘lanish bilan tabiiy gapirasiz, pasayuvchi, ko‘tariluvchi va pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang bilan ma’no ifodalaysiz hamda bir daqiqalik yozuvni shadowing usulida mashq qila olasiz.

scenes.title: Urg‘u, ohang va bog‘lanish
scenes.say: Hello again. Last time we built essays with a clear introduction, evidence and conclusion. Today we work on how you sound: stress, linking, intonation and shadowing.
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda esseni kirish, dalil va xulosa bilan tuzishni o‘rgandik. Bugun yozuvdan ovozga o‘tamiz. Dars oxirida siz so‘z va gap urg‘usini to‘g‘ri qo‘yasiz, so‘zlarni tabiiy bog‘laysiz, ohang bilan ma’no ifodalaysiz va har kuni qo‘llash mumkin bo‘lgan shadowing usulini bilib olasiz.
scenes.say_uz: Yana salom. Oldingi safar esseni aniq kirish, dalil va xulosa bilan tuzdik. Bugun qanday eshitilishingiz ustida ishlaymiz: urg‘u, bog‘lanish, ohang va shadowing.

scenes.title: Nega bu muhim?
board: Wrong stress → listeners may not understand you
English rhythm: stressed syllables are long and clear
scenes.say: Native listeners rely on stress to recognise words. A word with perfect sounds but the wrong stress can be harder to understand than a word with a slight accent.
scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida tinglovchi so‘zni avvalo urg‘usidan taniydi. Tovushlar to‘g‘ri, lekin urg‘u noto‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, so‘z tushunarsiz bo‘lib qolishi mumkin. Ingliz ritmida urg‘uli bo‘g‘in uzun va aniq, urg‘usiz bo‘g‘in esa qisqa va ko‘pincha “ə” tovushiga aylanadi. O‘zbek tilida bo‘g‘inlar ancha teng aytiladi, shuning uchun bu farqni ataylab mashq qilish kerak.
scenes.say_uz: Ona tilida so‘zlashuvchilar so‘zni urg‘udan taniydi. Tovushlari mukammal, lekin urg‘usi noto‘g‘ri so‘zni tushunish yengil aksentli so‘zdan qiyinroq bo‘lishi mumkin.

scenes.title: So‘z urg‘usi va schwa
scenes.say: Listen: photograph, photography, photographic. The stress moves, and the vowels change with it. Unstressed vowels often become the schwa, a short, relaxed sound.
scenes.say_native: Bir oiladagi so‘zlarda urg‘u ko‘chib yuradi. PHOtograph, phoTOgraphy, photoGRAphic. Urg‘u ko‘chganda unlilar ham o‘zgaradi: urg‘uli bo‘g‘in aniq, urg‘usizlari esa “ə” ga, ya’ni schwa tovushiga aylanadi. Schwa ingliz tilidagi eng ko‘p uchraydigan unli. U qisqa, bo‘sh, og‘iz deyarli ochilmaydi. Yozuvda esa u a, e, o, u harflarining istalgani bilan berilishi mumkin.
scenes.say_uz: Tinglang: photograph, photography, photographic. Urg‘u ko‘chadi va unlilar ham u bilan o‘zgaradi. Urg‘usiz unlilar ko‘pincha schwa, ya’ni qisqa va bo‘sh tovushga aylanadi.

scenes.title: Qo‘shimchalar urg‘uni boshqaradi
scenes.say: Some suffixes control stress. With tion, sion, ic and ical, the stress falls on the syllable just before them: information, decision, economic, political. Ity works the same way: university.
scenes.say_native: Ba’zi qo‘shimchalar urg‘uni o‘zi belgilaydi. -tion, -sion, -ic, -ical va -ity bilan tugaydigan so‘zlarda urg‘u qo‘shimchadan oldingi bo‘g‘inga tushadi: inforMAtion, deCIsion, ecoNOMic, poLItical, uniVERsity. Bu qoida juda ishonchli va B2 lug‘atidagi yuzlab so‘zni qamrab oladi. Yangi so‘z o‘rganganda oxiriga qarang.
scenes.say_uz: Ba’zi qo‘shimchalar urg‘uni boshqaradi. -tion, -sion, -ic va -ical bilan urg‘u ulardan oldingi bo‘g‘inga tushadi. -ity ham shunday: university.

scenes.title: Ot va fe’l juftliklari

examples.t: They want to reCORD a new REcord.
I obJECT to this OBject being here.
examples.uz: Bu buyum shu yerda turishiga qarshiman.

scenes.say: In many two-syllable pairs, the noun is stressed on the first syllable and the verb on the second: a record, to record; a present, to present; an increase, to increase.
scenes.say_native: Ikki bo‘g‘inli ko‘p juftliklarda ot birinchi, fe’l ikkinchi bo‘g‘inga urg‘u oladi. REcord, ya’ni yozuv yoki rekord, reCORD esa yozib olmoq. PREsent sovg‘a, preSENT taqdim etmoq. INcrease o‘sish, inCREASE oshirmoq. Imlo bir xil, faqat urg‘u ma’noni ajratadi. Fe’ldagi birinchi bo‘g‘in ko‘pincha kuchsiz: rɪˈkɔːd.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘p ikki bo‘g‘inli juftliklarda ot birinchi, fe’l ikkinchi bo‘g‘inga urg‘u oladi: REcord va reCORD, PREsent va preSENT, INcrease va inCREASE.

scenes.title: Urg‘udagi tipik xatolar
scenes.say: Watch these words: develop, comfortable, interesting, vegetable. In the last three, a whole syllable often disappears in natural speech: comfterble, intresting, vejtable.
scenes.say_native: Bu so‘zlarda ko‘p adashiladi, ko‘pincha rus tili ta’sirida: “комфортабельный”, “интересный”. To‘g‘risi: deVElop, COMfortable, INteresting, VEGetable. Oxirgi uchtasida tabiiy nutqda butun bo‘g‘in tushib qoladi: COMftəbl, INtrəstɪŋ, VEJtəbl. Shuning uchun ularni yozilishiga qarab bo‘g‘inma-bo‘g‘in o‘qimang.
scenes.say_uz: Bu so‘zlarga e’tibor bering: develop, comfortable, interesting, vegetable. Oxirgi uchtasida tabiiy nutqda butun bir bo‘g‘in ko‘pincha tushib qoladi.

scenes.title: Urg‘uni belgilang
scenes.say: Say each word aloud and mark the stressed syllable: photography, economic, record as a verb, and comfortable.
scenes.say_native: To‘rt so‘zni baland ovozda ayting va urg‘uli bo‘g‘inning tagiga chizing. Bugungi qoidalarni eslang: -ic qo‘shimchasi, ot va fe’l juftligi, va bo‘g‘in tushib qolishi. Har bir so‘zni ikki marta ayting: avval sekin, keyin tabiiy tezlikda, urg‘usiz bo‘g‘inlarni qisqartirib.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir so‘zni baland ovozda ayting va urg‘uli bo‘g‘inni belgilang: photography, economic, fe’l sifatida record va comfortable.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say: Photography. Economic. To record. Comfortable.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: phoTOgraphy, chunki photograph’dan farqli, urg‘u ikkinchi bo‘g‘inda. Ikki: ecoNOMic, -ic dan oldingi bo‘g‘in. Uch: reCORD, fe’l bo‘lgani uchun ikkinchi bo‘g‘in. To‘rt: COMfortable, birinchi bo‘g‘in va “for” deyarli eshitilmaydi. Agar xato qilgan bo‘lsangiz, so‘zni besh marta to‘g‘ri urg‘u bilan takrorlang.
scenes.say_uz: Photography. Economic. To record. Comfortable.

scenes.title: Gap urg‘usi va ritm
board: Content words stressed: nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs
Function words weak: a, the, to, of, and, can
I WANT to GO to the SHOPS.

examples.t: I WANT to GO to the SHOPS.

scenes.say: In sentences, we stress content words: nouns, main verbs, adjectives and adverbs. Function words like to, the and of are weak and quick. I want to go to the shops.
scenes.say_native: Gapda ma’no tashuvchi so‘zlar urg‘u oladi: ot, asosiy fe’l, sifat va ravish. Yordamchi so‘zlar, ya’ni a, the, to, of, and, can, kuchsiz va tez aytiladi. “I WANT to GO to the SHOPS” gapida uchta zarb bor, qolgan so‘zlar ular orasiga siqiladi. Shuning uchun ingliz nutqi o‘ziga xos ritmga ega va urg‘uli so‘zlar oralig‘i taxminan teng eshitiladi.
scenes.say_uz: Gapda mazmunli so‘zlar urg‘u oladi: ot, asosiy fe’l, sifat va ravish. To, the, of kabi yordamchi so‘zlar kuchsiz va tez aytiladi.

scenes.title: Ma’noni o‘zgartiruvchi urg‘u
board: Contrastive stress: stress the new or contrasting word
A: Is it a red car?  B: No, it’s a BLUE car.
A: Did Tom call?  B: No, ANNA called.

examples.t: I didn’t say she stole it.

scenes.say: We also move stress to show contrast. If someone asks, is it a red car, you answer: no, it's a blue car. The stressed word carries the new information.
scenes.say_native: Urg‘u yangi yoki qarama-qarshi ma’lumotni ko‘rsatish uchun ham ko‘chadi. “Is it a red car?” savoliga “No, it’s a BLUE car” deb javob berasiz, chunki yangi ma’lumot rang. O‘zbek tilida bu vazifani ko‘pincha so‘z tartibi yoki “-ku”, “aynan” kabi so‘zlar bajaradi: “Ko‘k mashina-ku!”. Ingliz tilida esa so‘z tartibi o‘zgarmaydi, faqat ovoz kuchayadi.
scenes.say_uz: Qarama-qarshilikni ko‘rsatish uchun ham urg‘uni ko‘chiramiz. Kimdir qizil mashinami deb so‘rasa, yo‘q, ko‘k mashina deysiz. Urg‘uli so‘z yangi ma’lumotni olib keladi.

scenes.title: Bitta gap, uch ma’no
board: I didn’t say SHE stole it. → someone else did
I didn’t SAY she stole it. → but I thought it
I didn’t say she stole IT. → she stole something else
scenes.say: Listen. I didn't say SHE stole it. I didn't SAY she stole it. I didn't say she stole IT. The words are the same, but each sentence means something different.
scenes.say_native: Bu klassik misolga quloq soling. “SHE” urg‘uli bo‘lsa: uni boshqa birov o‘g‘irlagan. “SAY” urg‘uli bo‘lsa: aytmadim, lekin shunday o‘yladim. “IT” urg‘uli bo‘lsa: u boshqa narsani o‘g‘irlagan. So‘zlar bir xil, ma’no esa butunlay boshqa. Muhokama va bahsda bu vosita fikringizni aniq yetkazishga yordam beradi.
scenes.say_uz: Tinglang. U o‘g‘irladi demadim, uch xil urg‘u bilan. So‘zlar bir xil, lekin har bir gap boshqa ma’no beradi.

scenes.title: Qaysi so‘z urg‘uli?
board: 1) A: Do you live in London?  B: No, I WORK in London.
2) A: Is the meeting on Monday?  B: No, it’s on ___.
3) A: You’re Kate’s brother?  B: No, I’m her ___.
Say B’s answers with the right stress.
scenes.say: Say B's answers with the right stress. One: no, I work in London. Two: no, it's on Tuesday. Three: no, I'm her cousin.
scenes.say_native: B ning javoblarini to‘g‘ri urg‘u bilan ayting. Avval o‘ylang: savoldagi qaysi ma’lumot tuzatilyapti? Aynan o‘sha yangi so‘z urg‘u oladi, qolganlari kuchsiz. Birinchi gapda namuna doskada. Ikkinchi va uchinchi gaplarni o‘zingiz to‘ldirib, baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: B ning javoblarini to‘g‘ri urg‘u bilan ayting. Bir: yo‘q, men Londonda ishlayman. Ikki: yo‘q, seshanba kuni. Uch: yo‘q, men uning amakivachchasiman.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say: No, I WORK in London. No, it's on TUESday. No, I'm her COUsin.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: “WORK” urg‘uli, chunki “live” tuzatilyapti, London esa o‘zgarmadi. Ikki: “TUESday”, chunki kun tuzatilyapti. Uch: “COUsin”, chunki “brother” tuzatilyapti. Agar siz “LONdon” yoki “MEETing” ni urg‘uli aytgan bo‘lsangiz, tinglovchi nimani tuzatayotganingizni tushunmaydi.
scenes.say_uz: Yo‘q, men Londonda ISHLAYMAN. Yo‘q, SESHANBA kuni. Yo‘q, men uning AMAKIVACHCHASIMAN.

scenes.title: Kuchsiz shakllar
board: Strong form when stressed or at the end:
What are you looking AT? /æt/  Yes, I CAN. /kæn/

examples.t: A cup of tea for two. /ə ˈkʌp əv ˈtiː fə ˈtuː/
examples.uz: Ikki kishi uchun bir piyola choy.

scenes.say: Function words are usually weak: a cup of tea for two. But at the end, or when stressed, they are strong: what are you looking at?
scenes.say_native: Ko‘p yordamchi so‘zlarning kuchsiz shakli bor: to “tə”, for “fə”, of “əv”, and “ən”, can “kən”, was “wəz”. Ular gap ichida doim kuchsiz. Lekin gap oxirida yoki urg‘u olganda kuchli shakl ishlatiladi: “What are you looking AT?”, “Yes, I CAN”. Hamma joyda kuchli shakl aytish nutqni sun’iy va sekin qiladi.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘p yordamchi so‘zlarning kuchsiz shakli bor. To, for, of qisqarib schwa bilan aytiladi. Lekin gap oxirida yoki urg‘u olganda kuchli shakl ishlatiladi.

scenes.title: Bog‘lanish (linking)
scenes.say: Words join. A final consonant moves to the next vowel: turn it off. Between vowels, add a light w or y: go on, I am. And in British English: far away.
scenes.say_native: Tabiiy nutqda so‘zlar bir-biriga ulanadi. Undosh bilan tugagan so‘z unli bilan boshlanadigan so‘zga yopishadi: “turn it off” go‘yo “tɜː nɪ tɒf”. Ikki unli orasida yengil “w” yoki “y” tovushi paydo bo‘ladi: “go on”, “I am”. Britancha talaffuzda yozuvdagi “r” odatda aytilmaydi, lekin keyingi so‘z unli bilan boshlansa, aytiladi: “far away”, “for example”.
scenes.say_uz: So‘zlar ulanadi. Oxirgi undosh keyingi unliga o‘tadi. Unlilar orasiga yengil w yoki y qo‘shiladi. Britaniyada esa: far away.

scenes.title: Tushib qolish va o‘xshashlik
board: Elision: next door → /neks dɔː/, last night → /lɑːs naɪt/
want to → wanna, going to → gonna (speech only!)

examples.t: Did you see it last night?

scenes.say: Sounds also drop or change: next door, ten pounds, did you. Wanna and gonna are fine in speech, but never in formal writing.
scenes.say_native: Tovushlar tushib qoladi yoki o‘zgaradi. Ikki undosh orasidagi “t” va “d” ko‘pincha tushadi: “next door”, “last night”. Qo‘shni tovush ta’sirida o‘zgaradi: “ten pounds” “tem pounds” kabi eshitiladi. “Did you” “didʒu”. “Wanna”, “gonna” og‘zaki nutqda tabiiy, lekin rasmiy yozuvda mumkin emas. Bularni bilish ham tinglashga, ham ravon gapirishga yordam beradi.
scenes.say_uz: Tovushlar tushadi yoki o‘zgaradi: next door, ten pounds, did you. Wanna va gonna nutqda normal, rasmiy yozuvda emas.

scenes.title: Sekin va tabiiy
board: Slow: What do you want to do?
Slow: I’m going to ask about it.
Natural: /aɪm ˈɡənə ˈɑːs kə ˈbaʊ tɪt/
scenes.say: First slowly: what do you want to do? Now naturally: whaddya wanna do? Slowly: I'm going to ask about it. Naturally: I'm gonna ask about it, all joined together.
scenes.say_native: Avval sekin, keyin tabiiy tezlikda tinglang. “What do you want to do” tabiiy nutqda “wɒdʒə wɒnə duː” kabi eshitiladi: kuchsiz shakllar, tushib qolish va bog‘lanish birga ishlaydi. Ikkinchi gapda “ask about it” bitta uzun so‘zdek eshitiladi. Siz bunchalik qisqartirishingiz shart emas, lekin bunday nutqni tushunishingiz kerak.
scenes.say_uz: Avval sekin: nima qilmoqchisan? Endi tabiiy. Sekin: bu haqda so‘ramoqchiman. Tabiiy: hammasi bir-biriga ulangan.

scenes.title: Bog‘lanishdagi xatolar
board: ✗ Every word separate and strong: I. Am. Going. To.
scenes.say: Don't say every word separately; it sounds robotic. Don't add a vowel before s: say school, not eschool. And don't write wanna in essays.
scenes.say_native: Uchta tipik muammo. Birinchi: har bir so‘zni alohida va kuchli aytish, bu robot ovoziga o‘xshaydi. Ikkinchi: “s” bilan boshlanadigan undoshlar birikmasi oldiga unli qo‘shish, o‘zbekchadagi “istansiya” kabi: “ischool” emas, “school”. Uchinchi: “wanna”, “gonna” ni essega yozish. Ular faqat og‘zaki nutq uchun.
scenes.say_uz: Har so‘zni alohida aytmang, bu robotdek eshitiladi. S oldiga unli qo‘shmang: eschool emas, school. Essega wanna yozmang.

scenes.title: Bog‘lab o‘qing
scenes.say: Read these with linking. One: turn it off. Two: an hour and a half. Three: I'll ask about it. Four: not at all.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta iborani bog‘lab o‘qing. Avval har birida qaysi undosh keyingi unliga o‘tishini belgilang. Keyin ularni bitta uzun so‘z kabi, uzilishsiz ayting. Kuchsiz shakllarni ham eslang: “and” va “a” qisqa bo‘lsin. Har birini uch marta takrorlang va tezlikni asta oshiring.
scenes.say_uz: Bog‘lab o‘qing. Bir: o‘chiring. Ikki: bir yarim soat. Uch: bu haqda so‘rayman. To‘rt: arzimaydi.

scenes.title: Javoblar: bog‘lanish
scenes.say: Listen again: turn it off, an hour and a half, I'll ask about it, not at all. Each phrase flows like one long word.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar doskada. “An hour and a half” da “n” “hour” ga o‘tadi, “hour” dagi “r” keyingi unli oldida aytiladi, “and” esa “ən” bo‘lib qisqaradi. “Not at all” da “t” lar keyingi unliga o‘tadi: “no tə tɔːl”. Amerikada bu yerdagi “t” ko‘pincha yumshoq “d”ga o‘xshab aytiladi. Asosiysi, ibora uzilmasdan oqishi.
scenes.say_uz: Qayta tinglang: turn it off, an hour and a half, I’ll ask about it, not at all. Har bir ibora bitta uzun so‘zdek oqadi.

scenes.title: Dialog: kafeda
board: Listening 1: Sam and Lily at a café
Listen for weak forms and linking
scenes.say: Sam: What do you want to have? Lily: Just a cup of tea for me. I had a big lunch. Sam: Not even a piece of cake? Lily: Go on, then. Half a slice. Sam: I'll ask if they've got any carrot cake. Lily: Lovely. And can we sit outside? Sam: It's a bit cold, isn't it? Lily: Not at all. It's a beautiful afternoon.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi tinglash. Sam va Lily kafeda buyurtma bermoqda. Ikki narsaga e’tibor bering. Birinchisi mazmun: kim nima buyurtma qiladi va qayerda o‘tirishmoqchi. Ikkinchisi talaffuz: “a cup of tea for me”, “go on”, “not at all” iboralarida kuchsiz shakllar va bog‘lanishni eshitishga harakat qiling.
scenes.say_uz: Sam: Nima ichasan? Lily: Menga faqat bir piyola choy. Tushlikni ko‘p yedim. Sam: Bir bo‘lak tort ham emasmi? Lily: Mayli, bo‘pti. Yarim bo‘lak. Sam: Sabzili tortlari bormi, so‘rayman. Lily: Zo‘r. Tashqarida o‘tirsak bo‘ladimi? Sam: Biroz sovuq, shunday emasmi? Lily: Aslo. Ajoyib kun.

scenes.title: Savollarga javob bering
board: 3) Where does Lily want to sit?
4) How is “cup of tea for me” pronounced?
scenes.say: Answer. One: what does Lily order? Two: why doesn't she want much? Three: where does she want to sit? Four: how did you hear the phrase a cup of tea for me?
scenes.say_native: To‘rt savolga javob bering. Birinchi savolda ehtiyot bo‘ling: Lily avval faqat choy dedi, keyin fikrini o‘zgartirdi. Ikkinchi va uchinchi savollar tafsilot haqida. To‘rtinchi savol talaffuz haqida: “of” va “for” qanday eshitildi? Iborani o‘zingiz ham xuddi shunday aytib ko‘ring.
scenes.say_uz: Javob bering. Bir: Lily nima buyurtma qiladi? Ikki: nega ko‘p xohlamaydi? Uch: qayerda o‘tirmoqchi? To‘rt: bir piyola choy menga iborasini qanday eshitdingiz?

scenes.title: Javoblar: birinchi dialog
board: 1) tea + half a slice of (carrot) cake
scenes.say: One: tea and half a slice of cake. Two: she had a big lunch. Three: outside. Four: uh cup uv tea fuh me, with weak forms.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: choy va yarim bo‘lak tort. “Go on, then” bu yerda “mayli, ko‘ndirding” degani. Ikki: tushlikni ko‘p yegan. Uch: tashqarida. To‘rt: “ə kʌp əv tiː fə miː”, ya’ni “a”, “of” va “for” kuchsiz, faqat “cup”, “tea” va “me” urg‘uli. Shu ritmni o‘zingiz ham takrorlang.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: choy va yarim bo‘lak tort. Ikki: tushlikni ko‘p yegan. Uch: tashqarida. To‘rt: kuchsiz shakllar bilan.

scenes.title: Pasayuvchi va ko‘tariluvchi ohang
scenes.say: Falls are for statements, wh-questions and commands: where do you live? Rises are for yes-no questions and surprise: you're leaving?
scenes.say_native: Ohang ingliz tilida ma’no tashiydi. Pasayuvchi ohang: darak gap, “wh-” savollar va buyruq: “Where do you live?” Ko‘tariluvchi ohang: “ha yoki yo‘q” savollari va hayrat: “Do you live here?” O‘zbek tilida savolni ko‘pincha “-mi” qo‘shimchasi bildiradi. Ingliz tilida esa “You’re leaving?” so‘z tartibi darak gapniki, lekin ko‘tariluvchi ohang uni savolga aylantiradi.
scenes.say_uz: Pasayuvchi ohang darak gap, wh-savol va buyruqda. Ko‘tariluvchi ohang ha-yo‘q savollari va hayratda: ketyapsizmi?

scenes.title: Pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang va ro‘yxatlar
board: The food was ↘↗good… (but the service wasn’t)
scenes.say: A fall-rise suggests an unsaid but: the food was good. In lists, the voice rises, then falls at the end: apples, bread and milk.
scenes.say_native: Pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang aytilmagan fikrni bildiradi. “The food was good...” ohang oxirida ko‘tarilsa, tinglovchi “lekin” ni kutadi. Bu ohang muloyim e’tiroz va ehtiyotkorlik uchun ham ishlatiladi. Ro‘yxatda har bir element ko‘tariluvchi, oxirgisi pasayuvchi: “apples, bread and milk”. Pasayish ro‘yxat tugaganini bildiradi.
scenes.say_uz: Pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang aytilmagan “lekin”ni bildiradi. Ro‘yxatda ovoz ko‘tariladi, oxirida pasayadi: olma, non va sut.

scenes.title: So‘roq qo‘shimchalari (tag)
board: ↘ It’s cold, ↘isn’t it? → I expect you to agree
↗ You’re coming, ↗aren’t you? → I’m not sure, real question

examples.t: You haven’t seen my keys, ↗have you?

scenes.say: Question tags change meaning with intonation. A falling tag, it's cold, isn't it, expects agreement. A rising tag, you're coming, aren't you, is a real question.
scenes.say_native: Question tag, ya’ni gap oxiridagi kichik savol, ohangga qarab ma’no o‘zgartiradi. Pasayuvchi tag: “It’s cold, isn’t it?” men javobni bilaman, faqat rozilik kutyapman. O‘zbekchadagi “sovuq-a?”ga o‘xshaydi. Ko‘tariluvchi tag: “You’re coming, aren’t you?” men haqiqatan bilmayman. Bahs va muloqotda bu farq juda muhim.
scenes.say_uz: Question taglar ohangga qarab ma’no o‘zgartiradi. Pasayuvchi tag rozilik kutadi. Ko‘tariluvchi tag haqiqiy savol.

scenes.title: Bir tekis ohang
board: ✗ Flat “Thank you.” → sounds bored or rude
scenes.say: A flat voice can sound bored or even rude in English, even when your words are polite. Compare: sorry with a rise means please repeat; sorry with a fall means I apologise.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek o‘quvchilari ko‘pincha ingliz tilida bir tekis, past ohangda gapiradi. Ingliz tinglovchisiga bu zerikkan yoki hatto qo‘pol eshitilishi mumkin, garchi so‘zlar muloyim bo‘lsa ham. Ovoz diapazonini kengaytiring: “Thank you!” aniq pasayish bilan. Va farqni eslang: “Sorry?” ko‘tariluvchi, ya’ni qaytaring, “Sorry.” pasayuvchi, ya’ni kechirasiz.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz tilida bir tekis ovoz zerikkan yoki hatto qo‘pol eshitilishi mumkin, so‘zlar muloyim bo‘lsa ham. Ko‘tariluvchi sorry qaytaring, pasayuvchi sorry kechirasiz degani.

scenes.title: Ko‘tariladimi yoki pasayadimi?
board: 3) It’s a lovely day, isn’t it? (you expect agreement)
scenes.say: Rise or fall? Read the four sentences on the board aloud.
scenes.say_native: Har bir gap uchun oxirgi urg‘uli so‘zdagi ohang yo‘nalishini aniqlang: ko‘tariluvchimi yoki pasayuvchimi. Qoidalarni eslang: “wh-” savol, “ha-yo‘q” savoli, rozilik kutuvchi tag va hayrat. Keyin har bir gapni to‘g‘ri ohang bilan baland ovozda, ikki martadan ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘tariladimi yoki pasayadimi? Doskadagi to‘rt gapni baland ovozda o‘qing.

scenes.title: Javoblar: ohang
scenes.say: One: fall. Two: rise. Three: fall on the tag. Four: rise, to show surprise.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: pasayuvchi, chunki “what” bilan boshlangan savol. Ikki: ko‘tariluvchi, ha-yo‘q savoli. Uch: tagda pasayuvchi, chunki siz rozilik kutyapsiz. To‘rt: ko‘tariluvchi, darak gap shaklida, lekin hayrat bildiradi. Diqqat: ba’zi ingliz so‘zlashuvchilari “wh-” savolni ham do‘stona ko‘tarib aytadi, lekin pasayuvchi ohang asosiy qoida.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: pasayuvchi. Ikki: ko‘tariluvchi. Uch: tagda pasayuvchi. To‘rt: hayratni ko‘rsatish uchun ko‘tariluvchi.

scenes.title: Dialog: dam olish rejalari
board: Listening 2: Ben and Zara plan a weekend
Listen to the intonation: what do they really mean?
scenes.say: Ben: We could go to the coast on Saturday. Zara: Well, we could… Ben: You don't sound keen. Zara: It's just that the forecast is terrible, isn't it? Ben: Is it? I hadn't checked. Zara: What about the museum? Ben: The museum… Fine. But we're having lunch by the river. Zara: Deal.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash. Ben va Zara dam olish kunini rejalashtirmoqda. Bu dialogda ma’noning katta qismi so‘zlarda emas, ohangda. Zara “Well, we could...” deganda va Ben “The museum...” deganda ohangga quloq soling. Tag savolining ohangiga ham e’tibor bering: Zara javobni biladimi yoki yo‘qmi?
scenes.say_uz: Ben: Shanba kuni dengiz bo‘yiga borsak bo‘lardi. Zara: Xo‘sh, borsak bo‘lardi... Ben: Unchalik xohlamayotganga o‘xshaysan. Zara: Shunchaki ob-havo dahshatli, shunday emasmi? Ben: Shundaymi? Tekshirmagan edim. Zara: Muzey-chi? Ben: Muzey... Mayli. Lekin tushlikni daryo bo‘yida qilamiz. Zara: Kelishdik.

scenes.title: Ohang orqali ma’no
board: 1) Does Zara like the coast idea?
2) “The forecast is terrible, isn’t it?” – falling or rising tag?
3) Is Ben enthusiastic about the museum?
4) What do they finally agree on?
scenes.say: Answer. One: does Zara like the coast idea? Two: was her question tag falling or rising? Three: is Ben enthusiastic about the museum? Four: what do they finally agree on?
scenes.say_native: To‘rt savolga javob bering. Birinchi va uchinchi savollarga javob so‘zlarda emas, ohangda: “we could...” va “the museum...” qanday aytildi? Ikkinchi savolda Zara ob-havoni bilganmi yoki so‘raganmi, o‘ylang. To‘rtinchi savol yakuniy kelishuv haqida, uni to‘liq gap bilan ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Javob bering. Bir: Zaraga dengiz bo‘yi g‘oyasi yoqadimi? Ikki: uning tagi pasayuvchimi yoki ko‘tariluvchimi edi? Uch: Ben muzeyga ishtiyoqlimi? To‘rt: oxiri nimaga kelishishadi?

scenes.title: Javoblar: ikkinchi dialog
board: 4) the museum + lunch by the river
scenes.say: One: no, her fall-rise shows doubt. Two: falling, because she already knows. Three: not really. Four: the museum, and lunch by the river.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: yo‘q, “we could...” dagi pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang shubhani bildiradi, Ben ham buni sezdi: “You don’t sound keen”. Ikki: pasayuvchi, Zara ob-havoni biladi va rozilik kutadi. Uch: unchalik emas, “The museum...” ham ikkilanish. To‘rt: muzey va daryo bo‘yida tushlik, ya’ni murosaga kelishdi.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: yo‘q, ohangi shubhani ko‘rsatadi. Ikki: pasayuvchi, u allaqachon biladi. Uch: unchalik emas. To‘rt: muzey va daryo bo‘yida tushlik.

scenes.title: Shadowing nima?
board: Shadowing = repeat a recording at the same time, with a tiny delay
Copy rhythm, stress, linking and intonation
Like a shadow following the speaker
scenes.say: Shadowing means repeating a recording almost at the same time as the speaker, copying the rhythm and melody, not just the words.
scenes.say_native: Shadowing, ya’ni “soya” usuli: siz yozuvni tinglab, so‘zlovchidan yarim soniya ortda qolib, u bilan deyarli bir vaqtda takrorlaysiz. Maqsad faqat so‘zlarni emas, ritm, urg‘u, bog‘lanish va ohangni ham nusxalash. Bugun o‘rgangan hamma narsa shu bitta mashqda birlashadi. Bu usul talaffuzni tez yaxshilaydi, chunki og‘iz va quloq birga ishlaydi.
scenes.say_uz: Shadowing yozuvni so‘zlovchi bilan deyarli bir vaqtda, soyadek takrorlash demakdir. Siz faqat so‘zlarni emas, ritm, urg‘u, bog‘lanish va ohangni ham nusxalaysiz.

scenes.title: Shadowing bosqichlari
board: 2 Listen; mark stress, linking, ↗↘ on the transcript
3 Shadow with the transcript, then without
scenes.say: Choose one minute of audio with a transcript. Listen and mark stress, linking and intonation. Shadow it with the text, then without. Finally, record yourself and compare.
scenes.say_native: Bosqichma-bosqich. Birinchi: matni bor bir daqiqalik yozuv tanlang, masalan podkast yoki qisqa nutq. Ikkinchi: tinglab, matnda urg‘uli so‘zlarni, bog‘lanishni va ohang yo‘nalishini belgilang. Uchinchi: avval matnga qarab, keyin matnsiz soyadek takrorlang. To‘rtinchi: ovozingizni yozib, asl yozuv bilan solishtiring va bitta farqni tuzating.
scenes.say_uz: Matni bor bir daqiqalik audio tanlang. Tinglab, urg‘u, bog‘lanish va ohangni belgilang. Avval matn bilan, keyin matnsiz takrorlang. Oxirida ovozingizni yozib solishtiring.

scenes.title: Samarali shadowing maslahatlari
board: 10 minutes a day > 1 hour a week
One speaker, one accent you like
Short chunks: one sentence at a time at first
Fix one thing per session (e.g. weak forms)
scenes.say: Ten minutes a day works better than an hour a week. Choose one speaker with an accent you like. Start with short chunks, and focus on one feature per session.
scenes.say_native: Bir nechta maslahat. Haftada bir soatdan ko‘ra har kuni o‘n daqiqa samaraliroq. Bitta so‘zlovchini, yoqqan aksentni tanlang va bir muddat o‘zgartirmang: britancha yoki amerikancha, lekin aralash emas. Avval bitta gapdan boshlang. Har bir mashg‘ulotda bitta jihatga e’tibor bering: bugun kuchsiz shakllar, ertaga ohang.
scenes.say_uz: Haftada bir soatdan ko‘ra har kuni o‘n daqiqa yaxshiroq. Aksenti sizga yoqqan bitta so‘zlovchini tanlang. Qisqa bo‘laklardan boshlang va har mashg‘ulotda bitta jihatga e’tibor bering.

scenes.title: Shadowingdagi xatolar
board: ✗ Material too fast or too hard
✗ Reading the text silently instead of speaking
scenes.say: Avoid these mistakes: material that is too fast, reading silently instead of speaking aloud, switching accents every day, and never recording yourself.
scenes.say_native: To‘rt xato. Birinchi: juda tez yoki qiyin material, natijada faqat g‘o‘ldiraysiz. O‘zingiz 80 foizini tushunadigan yozuvni tanlang. Ikkinchi: matnni ichingizda o‘qish, shadowing faqat ovoz chiqarib bo‘ladi. Uchinchi: har kuni boshqa aksent. To‘rtinchi: o‘zingizni hech qachon yozib olmaslik. Yozuvsiz qayerda xato qilayotganingizni bilmaysiz.
scenes.say_uz: Bu xatolardan qoching: juda tez material, ovoz chiqarmay ichda o‘qish, har kuni aksent almashtirish va o‘zingizni hech qachon yozib olmaslik.

scenes.title: Shadowing: birinchi urinish
board: I used to think pronunciation was about sounds.
But actually, it’s about rhythm and melody.
Once I started shadowing, people understood me much more easily.
scenes.say: Shadow me. I used to think pronunciation was about sounds. But actually, it's about rhythm and melody. Once I started shadowing, people understood me much more easily.
scenes.say_native: Endi birga mashq qilamiz. Doskadagi uch gapni o‘qib chiqing, keyin yozuv bilan birga, yarim soniya ortda qolib takrorlang. Urg‘uli so‘zlarni kuchli, yordamchi so‘zlarni kuchsiz ayting. “Used to” “juːstə”, “about” va “and” qisqa. Kamida uch marta takrorlang, oxirgisini matnga qaramay.
scenes.say_uz: Men bilan birga takrorlang. Ilgari talaffuz tovushlar haqida deb o‘ylardim. Lekin aslida u ritm va ohang haqida. Shadowingni boshlaganimdan keyin odamlar meni ancha oson tushuna boshladi.

scenes.title: Belgilangan matn
board: I USED to THINK pronunCIAtion was aBOUT SOUNDS. ↘
But ↘↗ACtually, | it’s aBOUT RHYTHM | and MElody. ↘
ONCE I STARted SHAdowing, | PEOple underSTOOD me | much more EAsily. ↘
scenes.say: Here is the marked text. Capitals show stress, bars show pauses, and arrows show the tone. Compare your version.
scenes.say_native: Mana belgilangan matn. Katta harflar urg‘u, chiziqlar qisqa pauza, strelkalar ohang. “Actually” dagi pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi ohang kutilmagan fikrni oldindan bildiradi. “Was”, “to”, “and”, “me” kuchsiz. “Started shadowing” va “understood me” bog‘lanadi. O‘zingiznikini solishtiring va bitta farqni tuzatib, yana bir bor takrorlang.
scenes.say_uz: Mana belgilangan matn. Katta harflar urg‘u, chiziqlar pauza, strelkalar ohangni ko‘rsatadi. O‘zingiznikini solishtiring.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: o‘zingiz gapiring
board: Say 4 sentences about how you learn English
1 contrastive stress (I don’t READ, I LISTEN)
1 question tag with the right tone
scenes.say: Now speak for thirty seconds about how you learn English, and record yourself.
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy amaliy topshiriq. Ingliz tilini qanday o‘rganayotganingiz haqida to‘rt gap ayting va ovozingizni yozib oling. Bitta qarama-qarshi urg‘u, masalan “I don’t READ much, I LISTEN”. Bitta to‘g‘ri ohangli tag savol. Va bitta ro‘yxat: ko‘tariluvchi, ko‘tariluvchi, pasayuvchi. Keyin yozuvni tinglab, uchala vositani topa olasizmi, tekshiring.
scenes.say_uz: Endi ingliz tilini qanday o‘rganayotganingiz haqida o‘ttiz soniya gapiring va ovozingizni yozib oling.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javob
board: I don’t READ much in English. I LISTEN.
It’s the best way to learn, ↘isn’t it?
Every day I shadow for ten minutes.
scenes.say: Here is a model. I don't READ much in English. I LISTEN. I listen to podcasts, songs and films. It's the best way to learn, isn't it?
scenes.say_native: Mana namuna. Birinchi gapda “READ” va “LISTEN” qarama-qarshi urg‘u oladi. Ikkinchi gapda ro‘yxat: podcasts va songs ko‘tariluvchi, films pasayuvchi. Uchinchi gapda tag pasayuvchi, chunki rozilik kutilyapti. To‘rtinchi gapda “shadow for ten minutes” ritmi aniq. Sizda ham shu vositalar bo‘lsa, vazifa bajarildi.
scenes.say_uz: Namuna. Ingliz tilida ko‘p O‘QIMAYMAN, TINGLAYMAN. Podkast, qo‘shiq va film tinglayman. Bu o‘rganishning eng yaxshi yo‘li, shunday emasmi?

scenes.title: Dars xulosasi
board: Word stress: suffixes, noun/verb pairs, schwa
Intonation: fall, rise, fall-rise, tags + shadowing
scenes.say: Today we covered word and sentence stress, linking and weak forms, intonation for meaning, and the shadowing technique.
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Birinchi: so‘z urg‘usi, qo‘shimchalar qoidasi, ot-fe’l juftliklari va schwa. Ikkinchi: gap urg‘usi va ma’noni o‘zgartiruvchi qarama-qarshi urg‘u. Uchinchi: bog‘lanish, kuchsiz shakllar va tovush tushishi. To‘rtinchi: ohang, ya’ni pasayuvchi, ko‘tariluvchi, pasayib-ko‘tariluvchi va tag savollar. Va bularning hammasini birlashtiruvchi shadowing usuli.
scenes.say_uz: Bugun so‘z va gap urg‘usi, bog‘lanish va kuchsiz shakllar, ma’no uchun ohang va shadowing usulini o‘rgandik.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Mark stress, linking and ↗↘ on the transcript
scenes.say: For homework, shadow a one-minute recording by a native speaker, record yourself and compare. Next time, we will practise debating and expressing counter-arguments.
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: matni bor bir daqiqalik ingliz tilidagi yozuvni tanlang, matnda urg‘u, bog‘lanish va ohangni belgilang, uni har kuni shadowing qiling. Oxirida ovozingizni yozib, asl yozuv bilan solishtiring. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida uchta farqni topish va ulardan bittasini tuzatgan holda qayta yozish. Keyingi darsda munozara va qarshi fikr bildirishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: bir daqiqalik yozuvni shadowing qiling, o‘zingizni yozib oling va solishtiring. Keyingi safar munozara va qarshi fikr bildirishni mashq qilamiz.

homework_uz: Matni bor bir daqiqalik ingliz tilidagi yozuvni tanlang, matnda urg‘u, bog‘lanish va ohangni belgilang, uni shadowing usulida mashq qiling, so‘ng ovozingizni yozib, asl yozuv bilan solishtiring. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida uchta farqni topish va bittasini tuzatib qayta yozib olish.

quiz.q: “They want to ___ a new album.” How is the verb stressed?
quiz.why_uz: Fe’l ikkinchi bo‘g‘inga urg‘u oladi: reCORD.
Urg‘u birinchi bo‘g‘inda va bir bo‘g‘in tushib qoladi.

quiz.q: Which words are normally stressed in a sentence?
options: content words: nouns, main verbs, adjectives

quiz.q: A: Is it a red car? B: No, it’s a ___ car. Which word is stressed?
What is the weak form of “for” in “a present for you”?
In British English, “far away” is pronounced…
“It’s cold, isn’t it?” with a FALLING tag means…

options: Repeating a recording almost at the same time as the speaker
Writing down every word you hear
quiz.why_uz: Shadowing yozuvni so‘zlovchi bilan deyarli bir vaqtda takrorlash.
